steps.b: In the Voice settings panel, choose the voice language first — it should match the language of your text. Then narrow the list with the gender filter or the search box (handy when you know a voice name). Ticking Speed or Pitch unlocks a slider plus a number box: speed runs from −100% to +100%, pitch from −100 Hz to +100 Hz. Preview a few voices before committing; two voices in the same language can sound completely different.

Type or paste into the big text box, or use Import File to load a .txt, .md or .text document. The counter at the top right tracks characters and lines as you type. Each generation takes up to 5,000 characters; split longer documents into parts. To insert a pause, type a break marker such as [break:500ms] or [break:2s] — or press Ctrl+B to drop one at the cursor. Plain punctuation is handled automatically: commas and full stops become natural pauses.

Preview Audio reads the text aloud instantly using a voice on your device, so you can sanity-check wording and pacing in seconds. Generate Audio renders the real thing on the server with the exact voice, speed and pitch you picked, in MP3 or WAV. Break markers are honored in the generated file (and quietly removed while previewing). If Autoplay after generation is ticked, each finished render starts playing by itself.

Every generated item lands in the Results list with its own player. Download the audio (MP3 or WAV, whichever you selected), and — because the engine reports word timings — matching subtitle files in both SRT and VTT formats, ready for video editors and players. Results live only for this browser session, exactly like a scratchpad: when you close the tab, they are gone, so download what you want to keep.

usecases.p: Add a clean voiceover to tutorials, explainers and shorts without booking a studio or a voice actor.
Turn chapters and long documents into listenable audio for learning on the move.
Draft episodes, intros and ad reads in minutes, then re-generate a line instead of re-recording it.
Make lessons, flashcards and readings accessible for students who learn better by listening.
Prototype prompts, greetings and responses for assistants and interactive voice apps.
Produce the same message in dozens of languages with native-sounding voices for each market.

faq.q: Is Text 2 Speech free to use?
faq.a: Yes. Listening, generating and downloading are free and need no account. Personal and learning use is fully covered; if you use generated audio commercially, make sure your use complies with applicable laws and the rights of any text you convert.

faq.q: Is there a character limit per generation?
faq.a: Up to 5,000 characters per generation (roughly five to seven minutes of speech). For longer material such as book chapters, generate it in parts and stitch the files — each render is faster, and re-doing one part is cheaper than re-doing a book.

faq.q: What can I type into the text box?
faq.a: Plain text in any of the supported languages, including mixed Chinese and English, numbers and common punctuation. Punctuation is interpreted for natural pausing and [break:…] markers insert exact silences. Emoji and symbols are read out by name, so remove any you don't want spoken.

faq.q: How do I add a pause?
faq.a: Insert a break marker anywhere in the text: [break:200ms] for a short beat, [break:2s] for two seconds. Pressing Ctrl+B inserts [break:500ms] at the cursor. Markers are silent in the output — you hear only the pause.
Audio in MP3 or WAV (chosen before generating), plus subtitles in SRT and VTT built from the engine's word-level timings — ideal for captioning videos with the same narration.

faq.q: Do my generated files stay online?
faq.a: No. Results exist only for your current browser session and are removed afterwards. Anything you want to keep, download before you close the tab.

about.h: Free text to speech online: what you get
p: Text 2 Speech converts typed, pasted or imported text into natural-sounding speech right in your browser. It is free, shows no ads and needs no account: choose a voice, add your text and press Generate Audio. Here is what the tool does, in plain numbers.

You can choose from more than 300 Microsoft neural voices in 75 languages, including regional accents such as American, British, Australian and Indian English, or European and Mexican Spanish. Filter the list by gender, search by name and play a short sample before you commit. Speed runs from −100% to +100% and pitch from −100 Hz to +100 Hz, so a single voice can sound calmer, brisker, deeper or brighter. Browse the [complete list of voices and languages](/voices.html), or read [how to choose a voice and accent](/guides/choose-voice.html) for your audience.

s.h: Download text to speech as MP3 or WAV
p: Every generation gives you a file to keep, not just playback in the page. MP3 (48 kbps, 24 kHz mono) is compact and plays on any phone, laptop or video editor. WAV (16-bit PCM, 24 kHz mono) is uncompressed, which suits further editing and mastering. With each file you also get SRT and VTT subtitles built from the word timings, so captions line up with the narration. Follow the [text to MP3 guide](/guides/text-to-mp3.html) for a step-by-step walkthrough, or the [AI voiceover guide](/guides/ai-voiceover.html) to narrate a video.

s.h: Text to speech with no sign-up
p: There is no registration, email address or login: open the page and start converting in any modern browser, on a phone, tablet or computer. Finished items appear in a results list for the current browser tab, each with its own player and download buttons. Close the tab and the list is gone, so save what you need first. The site is free to use and carries no ads; optional donations through Stripe or Buy Me a Coffee help pay for running it.

One generation takes up to 5,000 characters. In our test on 31 October 2026, 5,000 characters of English became about 5 minutes 28 seconds of audio and were ready in about 12 seconds. Split longer texts, such as book chapters, into parts and generate them one after another. You can insert up to 25 pause markers such as [break:2s] per generation, each up to 30 seconds and no more than 60 seconds in total, and import .txt, .md or .text files instead of pasting.

To create the audio, your text is sent to Microsoft's online speech service, so leave out anything confidential. Generated files are deleted from the server about 2 hours after your last generation. Have a question about formats, pauses or playback? The [help centre](/help.html) answers the most common ones.
